episode.comment: step cap = multiplier x number of passable cells; final value recorded here per the spec

energy.comment: every step burns 1 energy (bumps included); entering a penalty cell drains penalty_drain extra; at 0 the episode terminates as a death worth death_reward, costlier than any plausible continued struggle so giving up early is never optimal. initial=100 set by a learnability study: at the knife-edge budget 57 (optimal success 98.8%) tabular learners cap out near 84% eval success even with 80k episodes because every extra step converts to deaths, and sparse learners never ignite; at 100 shaped Q-Learning reaches 100% and sparse SARSA(0.7) 99% eval success. The low-energy policy structure (pit detours below e=15) is independent of the starting budget and remains in the analysis

sparse.comment: door_pass is 0 because a repeatable positive bonus on a non-terminal cell could be farmed by looping through the open door; the event is still logged

shaped.shaping: potential-based: F = gamma * phi(s') - phi(s) with phi = -scale * (remaining BFS distance of the mission: dist to key + key-to-goal if key not held, else dist to goal)

q_learning.comment: budgets x3 vs the gate design: the state space is ~17x larger (47066 states) and death caps episodes at ~100 steps, so each early episode yields far fewer samples than a 699-step timeout episode did. Sparse one-step Q-Learning never learns this task (documented in the report); the canonical agent is shaped/exponential

transfer.comment: epsilon starts at 0.3 for ALL scenarios (incl. scratch): zero-init Q with random tie-breaking explores like epsilon=1 anyway, and a low epsilon keeps the jumpstart advantage of transferred tables visible during training. Training uses the shaped reward (sparse is unlearnable from scratch under the energy budget); the source table is the shaped Q-Learning table and every evaluation runs on the sparse env
